args.message:
Fix round_money to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding) per FIN-212

The docstring claimed banker's rounding per FIN-212 but the
implementation used ROUND_HALF_UP, causing tests/test_money.py to
fail in the nightly build. Switch to ROUND_HALF_EVEN so midway
values round to the nearest even cent.

args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` was using `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite its docstring claiming to implement banker's rounding.

## Changes
- `src/money.py`: switched `round_money` to use `decimal.ROUND_HALF_EVEN` so halfway values round to the nearest even cent (e.g. `2.675 -> 2.68`, `2.665 -> 2.66`).

## Testing
- CI run `ci-0001` on this branch passed (tests/test_money.py green).

Fixes the nightly build failure.

transcript.content: The docstring says HALF_EVEN but the code uses ROUND_HALF_UP. I'll create a branch and fix it.
transcript.reasoning_content: The test expects 2.675 → 2.68 (2.68 within 2 decimals: 2.675 quantize to 0.01 — half, rounds to even → 2.68? 2.675 → third decimal is 5, second decimal digit is 7 (odd), so HALF_EVEN rounds to 2.68. And 2.665 → second digit 6 even, so 2.66. So fix is just replace ROUND_HALF_UP with ROUND_HALF_EVEN.
